confirmed: Read all 262 lines of the local markdown conversion, all 14 PDF pages, and Figures 1-6; the PDF ends with references on pp. 13-14 and contains no appendix or stated supplement.

The source is the published journal article by Moufida Boumous in Rupkatha Journal, volume 16, number 3 (2024), first published 27 October 2024; the title, author, publication date, and 14-page length recorded in the form match the document (PDF p. 1; page count and headers).

The study is described as a controlled between-subjects experiment, but allocation is only described as division into groups; no randomization mechanism is reported. has_randomized_people_study is false because no such study is confirmed, not because nonrandom assignment is demonstrated; assignment.randomized = not_stated, design_class = other, context_class = none, and core = unclear remain appropriate (PDF p. 5, section 3; p. 6, section 3.2).

The reported study sample is 60 students, including third-year bachelor, Master One, and Master Two students in the Bookish Minds club; the abstract says they were divided evenly. These are people, and the paper gives no randomized count or exclusion flow (PDF p. 1, Abstract; pp. 5-6, section 3.1).

Output counts are ambiguous: the introduction describes sixty student-written stories, the procedure describes a distinct story in each of three sessions, and the originality discussion refers to 30 G2 stories. None of these establishes a final participant analysis denominator or a consistent total output count; leaving n_units null is justified (PDF p. 2, Introduction; p. 6, section 3.3; p. 10, Originality).

G1 participants used Claude to generate ideas, structure narratives, and refine their stories; G2 wrote without AI. The methods describe three ordinary club sessions of 50 minutes each, common story prompts, and handwritten drafts incorporating AI suggestions in G1; a Claude model version is not specified (PDF pp. 6-7, sections 3.2-3.3).

The rubric scores originality, atmosphere, tension build-up, and character depth from 1 to 5; rater identity and the scoring procedure beyond the rubric are not specified, so measure = null is appropriately cautious (PDF pp. 7-9, section 4 and Figure 1).
Originality reported string verified: G1 1.95 to 2.30 and G2 4.35 to 4.75, described as mean scores across the stories (PDF p. 9, section 4; p. 10, section 4.1 Originality; p. 11, Figure 3).
Atmosphere reported string verified: Claude AI 2.40 to 2.60 and human participants 3.65 to 4.00 (PDF p. 11, section 4.1 Atmosphere and Figure 4).
Tension build-up reported string verified: Claude AI 3.95 to 4.30 and human participants 2.45 to 2.60 (PDF p. 12, section 4.1 Tension Build-up and Figure 5).

The one-line finding correctly reproduces the originality and tension ranges and their descriptive directions, with group allocation unstated. The ranges are not confidence intervals; no SD, SE, inferential test, or p-value is provided for these comparisons (PDF p. 6, section 3.2; pp. 9-12, results text and Figures 2-6).

This is one original empirical study, not a synthesis, so pooled estimates, standardized effects, and synthesis study counts are inapplicable (PDF pp. 5-12, sections 3-4.1). The paper declares no conflicts of interest and no funding (PDF p. 1).
summary: Random assignment and final analyzed counts are not reported, so no randomized-people study is confirmed and the reported 60-student sample does not establish the analyzed denominator. The source version and all recorded score ranges match the PDF, but the form omits character depth and leaves supported contrast and timing fields blank.
